glossary.definition: A class or array meeting the language’s aggregate criteria and supporting aggregate initialization.
Replacing or modifying the value of an object whose lifetime already exists.
Access to an object without taking responsibility for its lifetime; validity depends on the owner.
Storage available to a container before reallocation is needed; not the number of live elements.
Using const-qualified interfaces to express and enforce intended nonmutation through those interfaces.
The class operation that participates in establishing a valid object during initialization.
An attempted access through a pointer or reference after the required target lifetime has ended.
Introducing a name and information about an entity so it can be used and checked.
A declaration that provides the entity’s defining body or storage as appropriate.
The class operation associated with ending an object’s lifetime and releasing its owned responsibilities.
Checking whether a syntactically representable candidate satisfies the application’s rules.
Controlling permitted operations so callers do not casually bypass the representation’s rules.
A controlled test input and expected outcome, often accompanied by a defined execution environment.
A range including its beginning and excluding its end, such as indices zero through size minus one.
Establishing an object’s initial state; distinct from assignment to an existing object.
A condition that an object or algorithm maintains at specified boundaries.
The tool that resolves compatible object-file and library references into an executable or library.
A conversion restricted by list-initialization rules because it may lose representational information.
A pointer value that does not designate an object or function; it must not be dereferenced.
A region of storage with a type and a lifetime; an object is not the same thing as a source-level name.
Responsibility for ending a resource lifetime and releasing its associated storage or handle.
Interpreting input according to a grammar to form values or candidate operations.
An object whose value can designate another object or function, a permitted boundary, or no object; validity requires more than non-nullness.
A promised property after an operation completes under its documented conditions.
A requirement that must hold before an operation is used under its contract.
Source transformation involving directives, includes, and macros before later compilation stages.
Resource Acquisition Is Initialization: tying resource management to object lifetime, developed fully in Book II.
Changing internal organization while preserving the intended observable behavior.
An alias bound to an existing object or function; a reference does not by itself own the referent.
A retained check intended to detect a behavior defect returning after a change.
Compiler/runtime instrumentation that detects selected kinds of defects along executed paths.
The region in which a name can be found by the language’s name-lookup rules.
Conditional evaluation of the right operand of built-in logical AND or OR based on the left operand.
The category governing how storage is provided and retained, such as automatic, static, or dynamic.
A source file after preprocessing, including the declarations contributed by its headers.
Behavior for which the language imposes no requirements after a relevant rule is violated.
